zh.principle: **标准**：CMAC 认证模式（The CMAC Mode for Authentication）。摘要首句给出对象：「This Recommendation specifies a message authentication code (MAC) algorithm based on a symmetric key block cipher.」次句给出用途与产出：「This block cipher-based MAC algorithm, called CMAC, may be used to provide assurance of the authenticity and, hence, the integrity of binary data.」§1 把它安放在系列文件之中：「This publication is the second Part in a series of Recommendations regarding modes of operation of symmetric key block ciphers.」关键词行同样只列认证一面：「KEY WORDS: authentication; block cipher; cryptography; information security; integrity; message authentication code; mode of operation.」本文件规定 MAC 的生成与验证，不规定加密，也不规定密钥如何建立。
zh.why: 缺口是既有构造不可用：§3 写「The basic Cipher Block Chaining MAC algorithm (CBC-MAC) has security deficiencies [9].」并交代替代来源：「The core of the CMAC algorithm is a variation of CBC-MAC that Black and Rogaway proposed and analyzed under the name XCBC in Ref.[2] and submitted to NIST in Ref.[1].」改进链随后两句：「Iwata and Kurosawa proposed an improvement of XCBC and named the resulting algorithm One-Key CBC-MAC (OMAC) in Ref.[6] and in Ref.[5], their initial submission to NIST」与收束的「The OMAC1 variation efficiently reduces the key size of XCBC.CMAC is equivalent to OMAC1.」适用场景另有一句：「CMAC may be appropriate for information systems in which an approved block cipher is more readily available than an approved hash function.」即本文件的理由是补上分组密码侧的认证构造，而不是再造一种散列基 MAC。
zh.used: 义务写在编号章节，措辞分三级。§5.2 的两条 shall 限定底层密码与密钥：「The underlying block cipher shall be approved, and the key shall be generated uniformly at random, or close to uniformly at random, i.e., so that each possible key is (nearly) equally likely to be generated.」与「The key shall be secret and shall be used exclusively for the CMAC mode of the chosen block cipher.」密钥建立只到建议级：「To fulfill the requirements on the key, the key should be established among the parties to the information within an approved key management structure」。碰撞风险归运行系统：「For any system in which CMAC is implemented, the risk that an attacker can detect and exploit a collision shall be limited to a level that is appropriate to the value of the data.」三级措辞因此可分：算法与密钥是硬要求，密钥建立只是建议，把碰撞概率压到与数据价值相称的水准则落在部署一方的工程判断。
zh.broken: 四处限度各自不同层。§2 划出适用边界：「such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems.」§5.2 把密钥工作交出去：「the details of the establishment and management of keys are outside the scope of this Recommendation.」附录 A.1 承认认证保证有上限：「however, this assurance, as for any MAC algorithm, is not absolute.」并把短标签的条件写明：「A value of Tlen that is less than 64 shall only be used in conjunction with a careful analysis of the risks of accepting an inauthentic message as authentic.」附录 C 更直接说明本算法不管重放：「In some protocols an attacker may even be able to present to a verifier a message-MAC pair that the verifier itself generated earlier in the protocol.」即认证有效不等于来源方就是出示者，防重放须由协议另加序号、时间戳或 nonce。
zh.history: 这份文本顶部就是 NIST 的归档横幅：「The attached publication has been archived (withdrawn), and is provided solely for historical purposes.」横幅记下取代关系「The attached publication has been superseded by the following publication(s)」，其后继条目仍是 800-38B 与同一分册标题，作者与日期两行连读为「M.Dworkin Publication Date(s): October 6, 2016」；更新说明为「SP 800-38B is updated by the October 6, 2016 release of 800-38B, which includes editorial changes (as of October 6, 2016).」本体扉页连读为「NIST Special Publication 800-38B Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation: The CMAC Mode for Authentication Morris Dworkin」，日期行是 May 2005，引用行为「Natl.Inst.Stand.Technol.Spec.Publ.800-38B, 23 pages (May 2005) CODEN: NSPUE2」。本份正文不含免费获取的 DOI 行，横幅给出的标识符为 DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-38B。

en.principle: **Standard**: The CMAC Mode for Authentication (CMAC 认证模式). The abstract names the object in its first sentence: "This Recommendation specifies a message authentication code (MAC) algorithm based on a symmetric key block cipher." and the use in its second: "This block cipher-based MAC algorithm, called CMAC, may be used to provide assurance of the authenticity and, hence, the integrity of binary data." Clause 1 places it in the series: "This publication is the second Part in a series of Recommendations regarding modes of operation of symmetric key block ciphers." The keyword line carries authentication but no confidentiality: "KEY WORDS: authentication; block cipher; cryptography; information security; integrity; message authentication code; mode of operation." The document specifies MAC generation and verification, not encryption, and not how the key is established.
en.why: The gap is an unusable existing construction: §3 states "The basic Cipher Block Chaining MAC algorithm (CBC-MAC) has security deficiencies [9]." and names the replacement: "The core of the CMAC algorithm is a variation of CBC-MAC that Black and Rogaway proposed and analyzed under the name XCBC in Ref. [2] and submitted to NIST in Ref. [1]." The improvement chain follows: "Iwata and Kurosawa proposed an improvement of XCBC and named the resulting algorithm One-Key CBC-MAC (OMAC) in Ref. [6] and in Ref. [5], their initial submission to NIST" and closes with "The OMAC1 variation efficiently reduces the key size of XCBC. CMAC is equivalent to OMAC1." The setting is stated separately: "CMAC may be appropriate for information systems in which an approved block cipher is more readily available than an approved hash function." The argument is a block-cipher-side authentication construction, not another hash-based MAC.
en.used: The obligations sit in numbered sections at three wording levels. Section 5.2 constrains the cipher and the key with two shall requirements: "The underlying block cipher shall be approved, and the key shall be generated uniformly at random, or close to uniformly at random, i.e., so that each possible key is (nearly) equally likely to be generated." and "The key shall be secret and shall be used exclusively for the CMAC mode of the chosen block cipher." Establishing the key is advice only: "To fulfill the requirements on the key, the key should be established among the parties to the information within an approved key management structure". Appendix B puts a duty on the operating system: "For any system in which CMAC is implemented, the risk that an attacker can detect and exploit a collision shall be limited to a level that is appropriate to the value of the data." The levels separate cleanly: cipher and key carry shall duties, key establishment is should-level advice, and holding the collision risk to a level matched to the value of the data is left to the judgement of whoever deploys the system.
en.broken: The four limits work at different levels. Section 2 draws the applicability line: "such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems." Section 5.2 hands the key work over: "the details of the establishment and management of keys are outside the scope of this Recommendation." Appendix A.1 concedes the ceiling on assurance: "however, this assurance, as for any MAC algorithm, is not absolute." and conditions short tags: "A value of Tlen that is less than 64 shall only be used in conjunction with a careful analysis of the risks of accepting an inauthentic message as authentic." Appendix C is the plainest statement of what the algorithm does not do: "In some protocols an attacker may even be able to present to a verifier a message-MAC pair that the verifier itself generated earlier in the protocol." A valid MAC therefore does not identify whoever presented it, and replay defence is left to sequence numbers, timestamps or nonces in the protocol.

zh: message authentication code (MAC)：定长比特串，用来确立消息的真实性并因而确立其完整性。
CMAC：本文件规定的分组密码基 MAC 算法。
subkey：由密钥导出的秘密串，本文件中为 K1 与 K2，长度等于分组长度。
Tlen：MAC 输出 T 的比特长度，对同一密钥的所有调用固定。
OMAC1：Iwata 与 Kurosawa 对 XCBC 的精简，本文件称 CMAC 与之等价。
message span of the key：一把密钥下生成 MAC 的消息总数。
en: Message authentication code (MAC): a fixed-length bit string establishing the authenticity and hence the integrity of a message.
CMAC: the block-cipher-based MAC algorithm specified in this document.
Subkey: a secret string derived from the key, here K1 and K2, each one block long.
Tlen: the bit length of the MAC output T, fixed for all invocations under one key.
OMAC1: the refinement of XCBC by Iwata and Kurosawa, to which CMAC is stated equivalent.
Message span of the key: the total number of messages MACed under one key.
